research_rationale: Read the whole order (42 FR 58509, signed 1977-11-08): section 1 lets the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs continue monthly educational assistance when an institution closes between terms for not more than 45 days to conserve energy, exercisable once in any 12-month period per institution; section 2 requires the Administrator to advise beneficiaries of the effect on their entitlement. The order has no own-terms end. Held current law: the text of 38 U.S.C. 3680 (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09) now provides in subsection (a)(2)(A) that the Secretary may continue allowances while institutions are temporarily closed under an established policy based on an Executive order of the President or due to an emergency, capped at 4 weeks in any 12-month period, and its note prints this order. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes; current-law:usc hits the note, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog have no hit beyond the order. Authority statute checked in force: clause (A) of former section 1780(a), now 38 U.S.C. 3680(a), is in the held text. The 4-week statutory cap and the statute's use of the Secretary are changes made by statute to the underlying authority, not later presidential instruments, and are disclosed in the clause reason.
savings_reason: The order has no saving clause. Allowances already paid under it before any change in the statute are outside any held source. No instrument restoring or ending the policy was found by the three bounded searches, so the state is none after bounded search.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end. The order states no duration or date; the 45-day figure limits each closure, not the order. The later-events:ofr_catalog search has no hit and the bounded search of the held corpus for its number finds only the order's own printing and the 1989 codification. The held 38 U.S.C. 3680(a)(2)(A) refers to an established policy based on an Executive order, which supports continuation rather than an end.
scope_check: One clause (sections 1 and 2 read together). Section 1's authority is now exercised under 38 U.S.C. 3680(a)(2)(A), which names the Secretary of Veterans Affairs and caps continued payment at 4 weeks in any 12-month period; the order's 45-day figure therefore operates only within the statutory 4-week limit. That limit is a statutory narrowing, not an ending of the clause.

research_rationale: Read the whole order (81 FR 96329, signed 2016-12-23). It sets the order in which listed Department of Labor officials act as the Secretary of Labor under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act of 1998 (5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq.), excludes those serving only in an acting capacity and anyone not otherwise eligible, reserves the President's discretion to depart from it, revokes Executive Order 13245 of December 18, 2001, and disclaims private rights. It has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes and return zero hits for this order: no U.S. Code note or provision (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09), no CFR text (eCFR as of 2026-10-14) and no Office of the Federal Register disposition note names it. A search of the held corpus for the order's number finds only its own Federal Register printing and the Federal Register copy of the Department's own implementing notice, so no later instrument revoking, superseding or amending it is held. Limitation disclosed: the packet does not hold the current text of 5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq.; the Act is the order's cited authority and nothing held suggests repeal.
savings_reason: The only exhausted command is the revocation of Executive Order 13245 of December 18, 2001, which was complete on issuance; the superseded order stays revoked. No pending-matter residue was found by the three bounded searches, so the state is none after bounded search.

Its text says it is issued pursuant to Executive Order 13755 (replacing Executive Order 13245) and supersedes Secretary's Order 4-2008; it neither revokes nor amends any clause of Executive Order 13755, so no clause of this order ends on that date."}

research_rationale: Read the whole order (77 FR 31155, signed 2012-05-21). It sets the order in which listed Department of Commerce officials act as the Secretary of Commerce under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act of 1998 (5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq.), excludes those serving only in an acting capacity and anyone not otherwise eligible, reserves the President's discretion to depart from it, revokes Executive Order 13242 of December 18, 2001 and the Memorandum for the Secretary of Commerce of October 3, 2002, and disclaims private rights. It has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes and return zero hits for this order: no U.S. Code note or provision (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09), no CFR text (eCFR as of 2026-10-14) and no Office of the Federal Register disposition note names it. A search of the held corpus for the order's number finds only its own Federal Register printing and the Federal Register copy of the Department's own implementing notice, so no later instrument revoking, superseding or amending it is held. Limitation disclosed: the packet does not hold the current text of 5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq.; the Act is the order's cited authority and nothing held suggests repeal.
savings_reason: The only exhausted command is the revocation of Executive Order 13242 of December 18, 2001 and the Memorandum for the Secretary of Commerce of October 3, 2002, which was complete on issuance; the superseded order stays revoked. No pending-matter residue was found by the three bounded searches, so the state is none after bounded search.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end. Neither the order text nor any held later instrument states a date, condition or event ending the order of succession; the later-events:ofr_catalog search has no hit and the bounded search for the order's number finds only its own printing and the Federal Register copy of the same printing.
scope_check: Section 1 and each of its listed offices (Deputy Secretary through the Boulder Laboratories Site Manager) are separate scopes; section 2 narrows who may act and does not end any office; section 3 is a one-time revocation; section 4 disclaims private rights. No scope is limited by a later source; the same reason applies to every listed office because the order is a single ordered list and no held source changes any office.
independent_command_check: Independent command: section 3 revocation of Executive Order 13242 of December 18, 2001 and the Memorandum for the Secretary of Commerce of October 3, 2002, complete on issuance (2012-05-21). The remaining sections depend on the order of succession in section 1.
savings_check: No saving clause. No held source shows a continuing right or duty under the revoked instrument. State: none after bounded search.

research_rationale: Read the whole order (16 FR 11907, signed 1951-11-23): one paragraph delegating to the Secretary of State the President's authority under 18 U.S.C. 3496 and 3492(c) to prescribe consular-commission regulations and witness-fee schedules and to apply sections 3492-3496 to diplomatic officers, and revoking Executive Order 8298 of December 4, 1939. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes: current-law:usc (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09) hits the U.S. Code note printing the order under 18 U.S.C. 3496 with no ending statement; current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) hits 22 CFR 92.65 (authority line lists E.O. 10307) and 22 CFR 92.70; later-events:ofr_catalog has no hit. The held text of 18 U.S.C. 3496 still authorizes the President to prescribe those regulations. Limitation disclosed: the packet does not hold the text of 3 U.S.C. 301 (the general delegation statute cited in the order as the act of August 8, 1950); the delegated power itself rests on 18 U.S.C. 3496, which is held.
savings_reason: The order has no saving clause. The only surviving consequence is that Executive Order 8298 stays revoked; no held source restores it. No pending-matter residue was found by the three bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes), so the state is none after bounded search.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end. The order's own text states no duration, date or condition that ends the delegation. The later-events:ofr_catalog search has no hit for it, and the bounded search of the held corpus for its number finds only the 1989 codification, 22 CFR 92.65, 22 CFR 92.70 and the order's own printing; none revokes, supersedes or amends it.
scope_check: The sole paragraph is one clause with two delegations (18 U.S.C. 3496 regulations; 18 U.S.C. 3492(c) regulations for diplomatic officers) and one revocation sentence. Both delegations are read as continuing. The held 22 CFR 92.65 implements the commission-execution authority and cites this order in its authority line, which shows the delegation is still invoked in current regulations.
independent_command_check: The revocation of Executive Order 8298 is an independent command that was complete on issuance (1951-11-23): it needs no further performance, and no held source restores that order. It does not narrow or end the delegation, which is a separate continuing grant.
savings_check: No saving clause or transitional provision appears in the order. Acts done under Executive Order 8298 before 1951-11-23 are outside this order's text; nothing in held sources shows a pending right or duty under it. State: none after bounded search.
